quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: Two clauses in the perfect form: one positive and one negative.
quests.explanation: You heard exactly what was written. "Already" goes with the positive clause, and "hasn't" with the negative one.
quests.prompt: I've already sent the documents, but the manager hasn't confirmed receipt.
quests.sampleAnswer: I've already sent the documents, but the manager hasn't confirmed receipt.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say what you have already done and what you haven't done yet at work or school.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: Look at the short adverb between "had" and the verb.
quests.explanation: Just started means the concert was only beginning, and already started suggests we missed more of it. Both are past, but the feeling changes.
quests.prompt: By the time we got to the stadium, the concert had just started.
quests.sampleAnswer: By the time we got to the stadium, the concert had already started.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say when you arrived and what was happening by then.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A period of time is measured from a starting point.
quests.explanation: Exactly the same. "Since" points to a starting moment, and "has been working" shows it is continuing.
quests.prompt: She has been working at the same company since she left university.
quests.sampleAnswer: She has been working at the same company since she left university.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say how long she has been in her job, using since.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: The starting point of the wait is given by a time word.
quests.explanation: Ten and two are different clock times. Waiting since ten means a much longer, more annoying delay.
quests.prompt: We've been waiting for the plumber since two o'clock, and he still hasn't called.
quests.sampleAnswer: We've been waiting for the plumber since ten o'clock, and he still hasn't called.
quests.followUpQuestion: Complain about a wait, and say how long it has been.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A deadline is described with "by" and a future perfect form.
quests.explanation: "Will have finished" shows that the work will be complete at that point in the future.
quests.prompt: By next Friday, I will have finished all three chapters of my thesis.
quests.sampleAnswer: By next Friday, I will have finished all three chapters of my thesis.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say what you will have finished by the end of the week.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: How is the cooking described: a moment, or an activity in progress?
quests.explanation: Started cooking means the power cut came at the very beginning, while was cooking means it happened in the middle.
quests.prompt: I started cooking dinner when the power went out, so we ate cold sandwiches.
quests.sampleAnswer: I was cooking dinner when the power went out, so we ate cold sandwiches.
quests.followUpQuestion: Retell what you were doing when the power went out.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A question with "yet" checks for progress.
quests.explanation: "Yet" is used in questions and negatives to ask whether something has happened.
quests.prompt: Have you finished the report yet, or do you need another day?
quests.sampleAnswer: Have you finished the report yet, or do you need another day?
quests.followUpQuestion: Ask a colleague about progress, using yet.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: The sentence includes two past events. Which came first?
quests.explanation: Nothing was altered in this one. "Had already left" is the earlier event, and "got" is the later one.
quests.prompt: They had already left when I got to the station, so I took a taxi.
quests.sampleAnswer: They had already left when I got to the station, so I took a taxi.
quests.followUpQuestion: Explain what had happened before you arrived.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A frequency word appears early. How often?
quests.explanation: Never means zero times and rarely means very few times. The speaker's surprise is stronger with one of them.
quests.prompt: I've rarely seen so many people in this shop on a Monday.
quests.sampleAnswer: I've never seen so many people in this shop on a Monday.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say how often you see something unusual, in a full sentence.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A duration and a contrast: how long has she been learning?
quests.explanation: Three months feels natural for a beginner, and three years feels like a long time. The word "still" adds surprise.
quests.prompt: She's been learning the violin for three months, but she still can't read music.
quests.sampleAnswer: She's been learning the violin for three years, but she still can't read music.
quests.followUpQuestion: Compare her progress with what you might expect after that time.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: The sentence includes a time, a state and a consequence.
quests.explanation: "Was still sleeping" shows she hadn't woken up at the time of the call.
quests.prompt: When I called her, she was still sleeping, so I left a message.
quests.sampleAnswer: When I called her, she was still sleeping, so I left a message.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say what someone was doing when you called them.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A long sentence looks ahead to a completed task.
quests.explanation: "By the time" is followed by the present tense even when it refers to the future.
quests.prompt: By the time the results are published, we will have interviewed all the candidates.
quests.sampleAnswer: By the time the results are published, we will have interviewed all the candidates.
quests.followUpQuestion: Predict what will have been completed by a date you choose.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A decision is not final. A key word signals this.
quests.explanation: The recording follows the text word for word. "Yet" appears at the end of the clause in a negative sentence, and "whether" introduces the two options.
quests.prompt: I haven't decided yet whether to accept the offer or stay where I am.
quests.sampleAnswer: I haven't decided yet whether to accept the offer or stay where I am.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say a decision you still haven't made, and why.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A verb form describes the state of the shop when they arrived.
quests.explanation: Had closed means the shop was shut, and was closing means it was in the process. Could you still go in? Only one version allows it.
quests.prompt: The shop was already closing when we got there, so we went home.
quests.sampleAnswer: The shop had already closed when we got there, so we went home.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say what you saw when you arrived somewhere late.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A situation continues over a long period. Listen for the verb form.
quests.explanation: They are identical. "Have been trying" shows the effort has continued up to now.
quests.prompt: I've been trying to reach him all morning, but his phone keeps going to voicemail.
quests.sampleAnswer: I've been trying to reach him all morning, but his phone keeps going to voicemail.
quests.followUpQuestion: Describe your own attempt to reach someone.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A repeated complaint has a source at the end.
quests.explanation: Neighbours and street are different sources of noise, so the solution would be different too.
quests.prompt: Ever since she moved, she has been complaining about the noise from the neighbours.
quests.sampleAnswer: Ever since she moved, she has been complaining about the noise from the street.
quests.followUpQuestion: Complain about a noise, and say how long it has bothered you.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A future task will be finished by a certain time. Which room?
quests.explanation: The living room and the kitchen are different jobs, and the friend returning would walk into another room.
quests.prompt: We'll have finished painting the living room by the time you come back on Sunday.
quests.sampleAnswer: We'll have finished painting the kitchen by the time you come back on Sunday.
quests.followUpQuestion: Tell a visitor what will be finished before they return.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A moment of realisation happens in the middle of a walk.
quests.explanation: "I'd left" is a contraction of "I had left", which shows the keys were forgotten earlier.
quests.prompt: I was walking home when I realised I'd left my keys at the office.
quests.sampleAnswer: I was walking home when I realised I'd left my keys at the office.
quests.followUpQuestion: Tell the story of the moment you realised you'd forgotten something.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: The worry is linked to how long ago the person called.
quests.explanation: Since Monday might only be a couple of days, but since last week is longer and the worry seems more serious.
quests.prompt: He hasn't called since Monday, and I'm starting to worry.
quests.sampleAnswer: He hasn't called since last week, and I'm starting to worry.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say how worried you would be, and what you would do next.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: Two events are close together. Who was late?
quests.explanation: Text and audio match. "Had just pulled out" happened first, and "reached" came right after.
quests.prompt: The train had just pulled out of the station when I reached the platform.
quests.sampleAnswer: The train had just pulled out of the station when I reached the platform.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say who missed what, and how close it was.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: The intention is expressed with a verb in the middle.
quests.explanation: Texting and calling are different ways of contacting someone. The friend would expect a different message.
quests.prompt: I've been meaning to text you, but I keep forgetting to do it.
quests.sampleAnswer: I've been meaning to call you, but I keep forgetting to do it.
quests.followUpQuestion: Tell a friend what you've been meaning to do.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A question checks the situation now and compares it with an earlier time.
quests.explanation: "Still" and "has changed" show that the speaker is comparing then and now.
quests.prompt: Is the project still on schedule, or has something changed since Monday?
quests.sampleAnswer: Is the project still on schedule, or has something changed since Monday?
quests.followUpQuestion: Ask about the state of a project, and compare it with an earlier time.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: An intention is followed by new information.
quests.explanation: They are identical. "Was going to" shows a plan in the past that didn't happen.
quests.prompt: I was going to email you, but then I heard you were on holiday.
quests.sampleAnswer: I was going to email you, but then I heard you were on holiday.
quests.followUpQuestion: Explain what you had planned, and why it changed.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A period of time is introduced by a small word before the number.
quests.explanation: Almost twenty means slightly less than twenty, and over twenty means slightly more. The difference is a matter of accuracy.
quests.prompt: They've lived in this neighbourhood for almost twenty years, and they still love it.
quests.sampleAnswer: They've lived in this neighbourhood for over twenty years, and they still love it.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say how long someone you know has lived where they live.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A deadline is followed by the result that will be achieved.
quests.explanation: This is a straight match. "By six o'clock" gives the limit, and "will have finished" says the roof will be complete.
quests.prompt: By six o'clock tomorrow, the builders will have finished the whole roof.
quests.sampleAnswer: By six o'clock tomorrow, the builders will have finished the whole roof.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say what will be finished by tomorrow evening, as if you were the builder.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A frustrated speaker uses one small adverb near the start.
quests.explanation: Already suggests the speaker is annoyed that it took so many tries, and only says two isn't many. Both sound natural.
quests.prompt: I've only told him twice, but he hasn't done anything about it.
quests.sampleAnswer: I've already told him twice, but he hasn't done anything about it.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say something you have told someone more than once.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: The weather interrupts lunch. Listen to what the weather does.
quests.explanation: Stopped raining is good news and started to pour is bad news for people who are outside.
quests.prompt: We were having lunch outside when it suddenly stopped raining.
quests.sampleAnswer: We were having lunch outside when it suddenly started to pour.
quests.followUpQuestion: Describe a change in the weather that surprised you.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: A time expression explains why the speaker was so tired.
quests.explanation: All night is a single, very long night, and all week describes a whole week. The reason for falling asleep sounds different.
quests.prompt: I'd been studying all week, so I fell asleep during the exam.
quests.sampleAnswer: I'd been studying all night, so I fell asleep during the exam.
quests.followUpQuestion: Explain why you were tired, using the past perfect.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: Two pieces of news are packed together.
quests.explanation: No change. "Has just told" means very recently, and "has accepted" says the decision is made.
quests.prompt: She's just told me she has accepted a job in another city.
quests.sampleAnswer: She's just told me she has accepted a job in another city.
quests.followUpQuestion: Share some news you have only just heard.

quests.instruction: Listen and tilt to yes if the audio matches the text, or no if it doesn't.
quests.hint: The time is the moment that starts the mystery.
quests.explanation: Since the meeting started or ended points to a different time of disappearance, which changes the questions people ask.
quests.prompt: Nobody has seen the manager since the meeting started, and his phone is switched off.
quests.sampleAnswer: Nobody has seen the manager since the meeting ended, and his phone is switched off.
quests.followUpQuestion: Say when you last saw someone, and how you felt.
